text:
maria: Quick sanity check on a regional headroom sim I ran. Trying to quantify how much short-duration burst capacity we need vs committed GPU-hours for EU-west during shopping season. TL;DR: small bursts matter more than raw monthly GPU-hours for tail latency.
kevin: can you share the assumptions? e.g., token mix, concurrent reqs, and what you treat as a burst (30s, 5m?)
sanjay: I grabbed a 7-day baseline and ran a 1-in-100 peak scenario (roughly 3.2x baseline q95). Treating a burst as a 120s window for routing/queueing decisions. Key numbers: baseline EU-west steady = 320k tokens/s, normal conc reqs ~4500, avg tokens per request ~70.
maria: right — and GPUs are profiled as: 1 A100 equiv ~ 12k tokens/s for our mix (mixed seq lengths). So baseline capacity is ~26 A100 equivs (we round to 30 in-prod).
kevin: 120s makes sense. What's failure mode currently? backpressure to other regions or request drops?
capacity-bot: alert: last saturday 03:12 UTC experienced interregion egress spikes. Reroute rate to NA peaked at 18% -> latency +20% for routed requests.
olivia: last weekend we saw the EU cluster fill its burst queue and begin shedding at ~1.8x baseline because of cross-region bandwidth throttles. That shed behavior is what worries me for product SLAs.
sanjay: I ran two policies: (A) conservative: provision committed for 2.5x baseline (monthly cost up ~2.4x), rely on cross-region fallback for >2.5x; (B) mixed: commit for 1.2x baseline + a short-lived burst pool (spot/promo nodes + prewarmed instances) sized for additional 2.5x for up to 3 min. Results: B hits 95% tail latency SLAs in 98% sims, A hits 96% but costs more.
maria: can you paste the simple cost/throughput calc you used? want to sanity check math.
sanjay: sure — simplified snippet I used:
```
# tokens_per_gpu = 12_000 # tokens/s
baseline_tokens = 320_000
baseline_gpus = ceil(baseline_tokens / tokens_per_gpu) # -> 27
# Policy A commit_gpus = ceil(2.5 * baseline_tokens / tokens_per_gpu) # -> 68
# Policy B commit_gpus = ceil(1.2 * baseline_tokens / tokens_per_gpu) # -> 32
# burst_pool_gpus = ceil((2.5-1.2) * baseline_tokens / tokens_per_gpu) # -> 36
```
kevin: math looks right. But the burst pool being 36 GPUs for short duration — do we model warmup waste? cold startup can blow the cost advantage.
jamie: in our sims I added a 60s prewarm penalty per instance (partial tokens lost) and a KV-warm cache inefficiency factor of ~0.85 for first 90s. That ended up increasing effective burst need by ~10%.
capacity-bot: sim-run-1743219876: policy B (with prewarm) median cost delta vs A = -18%, 95th pct cost delta = -7%, SLA breach rate B=1.9% vs A=3.8%.
olivia: so mixed policy wins on cost and SLOs but is operationally more complex (managing spot replacement, prewarm hooks). Also need routing rules to avoid cross-region egress hitting cloud egress caps.
maria: what about routing shape? jamie had suggested a punting/queuing hybrid earlier.
jamie: yes — instead of immediate cross-region reroute at queue depth X, we hold 30s in a per-customer short queue (drop after 120s) and scale to burst pool from queue fill rate. That reduces unnecessary interregion egress and avoids flip-flopping. Sim shows interregion egress peak reduced by ~40%.
kevin: do we have a simple runbook for triggering burst pool vs bumping committed? e.g., if weekly p99 peaks exceed 2x for 3 consecutive weeks escalate to capacity commit review?
sanjay: propose: automated weekly headroom report + an alert if weekly p99 > 2x baseline AND avg burst duration > 90s -> flag for finance review and provisioning change.
maria: agree. Also: add a short-term dev task: instrument per-customer queue fill and KV-warm fraction so we can reduce the 10% fudge. Can someone own it? @kevin?
kevin: I can take it. I'll add metrics: queue_fill_rate, prewarm_efficiency, first_90s_token_loss.
maria: ok great. last asks: olivia, can you estimate monthly committed cost delta for policy B vs A for finance? put ballpark numbers (we'll round).
olivia: on it — I'll pull current committed pricing and include expected spot offsets. Expect B to be ~15-25% cheaper on monthly bill with lower headroom tail cost, but ops risk is slightly higher.
kevin: thanks — I'll instrument and feed sanjay's sim with observed loss numbers, then rerun sim in 48h.
maria: perfect. Appreciate the quick eyes. If capacity-bot posts the final sim artifacts drop them here and we'll move to a small RFC for the mixed-policy change. :white_check_mark:
